target_customer: Medical device makers (implant OEMs, surgical robot and navigation vendors, patient-specific device makers) that license planning and anatomy AI software
problem: Surgical planning from patient scans is slow and manual, and device companies need anatomy AI and planning software to make robots and patient-specific implants practical.
business_model: Software licensing to device companies as an API, white-label app or full stack

founders.name: Vikas Karade
founders.background_notes: Founder and CEO on the YC page; a 2025 interview calls him Dr. Karade. Education and employers not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Amit Maurya
founders.background_notes: YC page says over 10 years in medical software, AI and ML medical image processing, AR and VR surgical simulation, robotics and FDA-related work. No employers or education listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Medical image segmentation, 3D planning and robot registration need AI, imaging and regulatory-grade software for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Embedded in partner devices that hold the regulatory clearances, which creates integration lock-in, but no data or patent evidence was found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; the company licenses to device makers rather than competing with them.

market_need_then: Not documented in dated sources. The YC page describes robotics, AR navigation and cloud 3D planning as the original focus.

branding.domain_note: Currently uses algosurg.ai; history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical, partner-focused, scan to execution tagline

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand, community or merch found; B2B licensing business where partners hold the visible brand.

pivots.from: Own AI software for robotic surgery, AR navigation and cloud 3D planning
pivots.to: Licensing planning and anatomy AI to device companies
pivots.why: A directory profile says it licenses technology rather than marketing its own device; timing not stated

outcome_analysis: AlgoSurg is still active as a licensor of surgical planning AI. Its site claims a knee planning product on a partner robot platform in India with over 200 robots and more than 10,000 surgeries planned. No funding rounds or press on growth were found, so its venture trajectory is unknown.
notes: Funding: CB Insights lists about 120 thousand dollars total and Village about 460 thousand, both single aggregator figures, so unverified and not recorded as rounds. No dated competitor source near January 2018 was found; the only competitor list surfaced was for a different company, so the list is empty. No outcome or shutdown news found. Founding year conflicts: CB Insights says 2016 and a directory says the India entity was incorporated 2018-01-19; YC says 2018. Dr. title for Karade is from the 2025 interview. Company site names no founders; claims on traction are self-reported. Completeness pass: the round rests on a single database (Village, last round $200K, total $460K, backers Y Combinator and Plug and Play, no date). CB Insights lists a total of $120K, which conflicts. The Village total exceeds the recorded round, so other rounds may exist. No press announcement found.
